sentences.text: Klamelisaurus was a medium-sized sauropod dinosaur approximately 13 meters long, with its neck accounting for half of its total length.
The type specimen preserves nine neck vertebrae, with an estimated total of sixteen and a total length of 6.5 meters.

Moore and colleagues identified irregular, plate-like extensions on the spinoprezygapophyseal laminae of the neck vertebrae as a unique feature, alongside deep openings found on the sides below these laminae and in front of the spinodiapophyseal fossae.
The type species Klamelisaurus gobiensis was named by Zhao Xijin in 1993 based on a partial skeleton found in 1982, 35 km north of the abandoned town of Jiangjunmiao.

Preparation and restoration began in 1985 after transport to Beijing, and the specimen was redescribed by Andrew Moore and colleagues in 2020 after receiving limited attention following its initial description.

Zhao originally classified Klamelisaurus as the sole member of the new subfamily Klamelisaurinae within the order Bothrosauropodoidea, describing it as an early to middle stage sauropod possessing transitional characters.
However, phylogenetic analyses suggest Klamelisaurus belongs to the family Mamenchisauridae, a group of primarily Chinese sauropods.
This herbivorous sauropod lived during the Middle Jurassic, specifically the Oxfordian and Callovian stages, approximately 165 to 161 million years ago in the Shishugou Formation of China.

Researchers have debated whether Bellusaurus is a juvenile Klamelisaurus or a separate adult form. Moore and colleagues refuted the hypothesis that Klamelisaurus is the adult form of Bellusaurus, noting that the Klamelisaurus holotype comes from older rock layers and that the two were not contemporaries. They identified differences in vertebral pneumatic features between the two genera that cannot be explained by age differences, as Bellusaurus possessed specific pneumatic features in dorsal neural spines and arches that Klamelisaurus lacked. While bifurcated neural spines and wing-shaped processes on rear dorsals might vary with age, complicating the distinction, anatomical and geological age differences led to the rejection of the idea that Bellusaurus is a juvenile Klamelisaurus.
